youtube.baslik: How can a protein absent from hair cells cause hearing loss? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: The GJB2 gene encodes connexin 26, a protein that forms gap junctions in the cochlea; it is found not in hair cells but in supporting cells and the spiral ligament. These junctions help recycle potassium, and when they fail, maintenance of the endolymph environment is thought to be disrupted. Since the problem lies before the nerve, cochlear implant outcomes in severe loss are usually very good.
